To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the addition of Cr, Mo, and Al to Ni-Mn-CuC cast iron results in the formation of acicular ferrite with high hardness and abrasive-wearing resistance and good corrosion resistance.
The highest abrasive-wear resistance and the lowest depth of corrosion pits were obtained for the cast iron containing 2% Cr and 2% Mo and 0.4 Al, in the annealed state.

the addition of Cr, Mo, and Al to Ni-Mn-CCu cast iron in the heat-treated condition results in the formation of acicular carbon-supersaturated ferrite in the matrix of the castings, which significantly increases their hardness and abrasive-wearing resistance.

the possibility of increasing abrasive wear and corrosion resistances of Ni-Mn cast iron by introducing small amounts of alloying elements (Cr, Mo, Al) and subsequent heat treatment.
the possibility of improving the abrasive-wear and corrosion resistance of castings by the addition of Cr, Mo, Al and heat treatment.
the possibility of improving the properties of Ni-Mn cast iron by adding Cr, Mo and/or Al.

the addition of Cr and Mo to Ni-Mn-CU cast iron in the amounts of 0.2–1.0% and 0.2-1.0% respectively and an addition of 1.0% Al, in the as-casted state, results in a significant improvement of mechanical and corrosion properties of this alloy.
the addition of Cr and Mo to Ni-Mn-CU cast iron results in an increase of its hardness, abrasion and corrosion resistance.
, in Ni-Mn-Cr-Cu cast iron, Cr and Mo can be used as alloying elements, which improve the abrasive wear resistance and corrosion resistance of the alloy.

Ni-Mn-Cr-Mo-Al cast iron is a very good material for wear-resistant castings.
